hypothesis: Two real cases where boundary extraction needed phasing will indicate the build-trigger; skill-use log helps measure when this fires.
summary: A planning skill for staged boundary decoupling. Consumes a staging-decision-framework ADR + an /impact-feature output + a /propose-boundary artifact, then produces a phase-graph (nodes = phases, edges = predecessors) with phase-boundary verification gates and partial-revert plans. Build only after the staging-decision-framework ADR lands AND a real boundary extraction surfaces a P0 staging fork.
title: /plan-phased-refactor skill for staged decoupling

hypothesis: Coherence drift can be measured by cross-package change-amplification + cross-package import directionality + concept fingerprint overlap. Open question whether this rolls up cleanly enough to be actionable.
summary: Higher-abstraction analog to SOLID: detects when a system as a whole drifts from internal coherence. Cousin to /find-folder-topology-drift but at the system-of-subsystems level. Candidate signals: concepts fighting across modules, subsystem boundaries dissolved by features that cross them, change-amplification that crosses package walls.
title: System-coherence drift detector

summary: Backfill skill-use logging across every existing skill rather than opt-in-as-touched. Would give immediate full coverage but requires touching every skill's terminal stage. Trade-off: speed of evidence accumulation vs upfront instrumentation cost. Engineering-skills owns this question since the shared library is where skills land first.
title: Retroactive skill-use logging across existing ecosystem

hypothesis: Grouping by job (find/propose/refactor/map/decide/track/extract/etc.) will surface seams that motivate orchestration layers and reveal which large skills are split-candidates.
summary: Apply folder-organization conventions (>=3-sibling packaging threshold; see host project decision registry) to .claude/skills/. Today's catalog is flat (~30+ skills); natural groups exist (find-* / propose-* / refactor-* / map-* / decide / track-*). The conventions codified for the codebase should apply to the skill ecosystem itself.
title: Apply folder-organization rules to .claude/skills/

summary: Hash vs verbatim target paths; retention/rotation policy beyond the basic compaction-and-archive mechanism; commit-gate criteria for the active log. Defer until log size or commit pressure makes the question concrete. The compaction mechanism handles growth but not privacy.
title: Skill-use log privacy and retention policy

hypothesis: There is a missing midpoint between '/refactor-subsystem extracts N files' and 'leave it bad': a single-file reorganizer that clusters symbols by domain, adds banner comments + a top-of-file index, declares __all__, and emits no semantic changes. Many 1K-LOC omnibuses are tolerable when sensibly organized; not all need extraction.
origin: Conversation in host project 2026-05-14 on omnibus follow-up options
summary: Skill that takes an omnibus file as input and produces a structurally-reorganized version with: (1) symbol clustering by domain (reuse the same head-noun clustering /find-omnibus uses), (2) section banner comments grouping each cluster, (3) a top-of-file index/TOC docstring, (4) an explicit __all__ declaration listing the public API in order, (5) zero semantic changes. Default --require-recent-edits gate skips files with no edits in 90+ days unless --force ('leave stable files alone'). Outputs a --dry-run move plan first. Tooling caveat: a whole-file reorder buries git-blame trails — mitigated by 'git log --follow' / 'git blame -w -CC' which preserve authorship across moves; report should hint at these flags. Slots into the maintenance loop as a sibling to /refactor-subsystem: /find-omnibus → DECISION (decompose | reorganize | leave) → /refactor-subsystem OR /organize-file OR skip. Composes with: /propose-boundary (when reorg surfaces a clean seam, re-evaluate as a refactor candidate); the staged-boundary ADR (refuse-phasing rules apply if a reorg unexpectedly grows into a refactor).
title: /organize-file — reorganize an omnibus without restructuring

hypothesis: Two-token prefix or verb-stripping logic would surface the obviously-correct seams that humans see immediately. The current single-token approach is too eager to collapse.
summary: Naming clusters use first-token-after-generic-verb-strip as cluster key. e.g. 'save_html_to_file' and 'save_screenshot_to_file' both land in the 'save_*' cluster, but the real semantic cluster is 'file I/O' (which also wants 'url_to_filename'). The skill misses obvious file-I/O / crawl / discovery clusters when the head-noun is generic. Candidate fix: two-token prefix OR head-noun-after-verb extraction. Evidence: a real shared-helper file showed 3 weak prefix seams while manual reading shows >=3 strong semantic clusters.
title: /propose-boundary naming clusters are single-token-prefix only

hypothesis: Most real targets have lifetime > 90 days; the default should reflect that. A loud empty-signal warning + auto-widening would prevent silent quality degradation.
summary: Default --co-edit-days=90 returns 0 co-edit pairs for active code if all activity is older than the window (or the file was renamed and git log doesn't follow rename). Candidate seams then score co_edit_intensity=0.00; only naming signal carries. Candidate fixes: (a) default to 180+ days, (b) make window relative to file mtime, (c) warn loudly when co-edit signal is empty so the human knows naming-only scores are weaker evidence.
title: /propose-boundary co-edit signal empty when target has no recent git history

hypothesis: Every project with the Claude harness will have .claude/worktrees/ pollution. A default skip-glob is high-value, near-zero risk.
summary: Proposal for a shared helper listed ~150 importers; ~80% were duplicates from stale agent worktrees under .claude/worktrees/agent-*. These worktrees contain old copies of the codebase. Inflates importer counts, dilutes 'callers_into_private_helpers', and makes the report harder to scan. Candidate fix: ship with default --skip-path-glob '.claude/worktrees/**' (and maybe also '**/.venv/**' though Python AST should not import .venv anyway). Trivial change; broad impact.
title: /propose-boundary should default-skip .claude/worktrees/

hypothesis: find-omnibus already solved this with a JSON+md split; mirroring that pattern is the right move.
summary: --output accepts any path including X.md but writes a JSON data dump (multi-MB for nontrivial targets). Misleading filename suggests human-readable markdown. Candidate fixes: (a) rename flag to --output-json (consistent with find-omnibus's --output-md / --output-json split), (b) add a markdown renderer that consumes the JSON and produces a scannable report — same pattern as find-omnibus's report.py. (b) is the better fix because it preserves machine-readable data for downstream skills while also giving humans a readable surface.
title: /propose-boundary --output X.md writes JSON, not markdown

hypothesis: Augment the report with either (a) a verb-phrase summary per cluster ('formats *', 'sanitizes *') instead of bare nouns, or (b) a 5-line head-of-file summary the skill prompts the user to write before deciding. Either way, the cluster-name column should not be the primary disambiguator — risk score plus a one-line semantic hint should be.
summary: Top-N omnibus shortlist showed cluster names that didn't match the real concerns of the file. A high-LOC export file reported clusters as 'iter, export, notes, flatteneddata' — but the architect-skim concerns were dimension-formatting, image-sanitization, cross-DB JOIN, and downstream wiring. The detector picks the most frequent head-nouns, not the semantically distinct concerns. Result: humans have to open the file to know whether decompose vs reorganize is the right call.
title: /propose-boundary cluster names hide intent on dense files

hypothesis: Path(__file__).parent / 'literal' is a Python idiom; every Python project with refactors will eventually hit this bit-rot. The skill is one of the cheapest guardrails available.
summary: Host project shipped a /find-broken-file-refs skill (advisory SUSPECT scan for Python Path(__file__).parent / 'literal' expressions whose target doesn't exist on disk). Catches refactor-induced bit-rot in self-anchored asset paths. SKILL.md currently references Django render() in not_for; needs scrubbing for the engineering-skills mirror (Python-general, framework-agnostic). Pairs with ADR 0015 (refactor-asset-path-verification). Skill scope is universally applicable to any Python codebase with relocatable modules + literal-asset paths.
title: Mirror /find-broken-file-refs skill (host: pnci-pricing → engineering-skills)

hypothesis: Asset-path bit-rot is a universal Python refactor failure mode. A template ADR + the suspect skill together close it cheaply.
summary: Host project shipped ADR 0015: every Python file move must prove Path(__file__) constants still resolve. Decision is anchored by two real production incidents where modules moved a directory deeper and their .parent chain silently resolved to the wrong location, with the failure surfacing only at runtime. Engineering-skills mirror should be the template form (decision sections present, concrete N thresholds/incident IDs replaced with placeholders for adopters to fill in). Pairs with /find-broken-file-refs intake and /refactor-subsystem Phase 6.0.5 gate.
title: Mirror ADR 0015 (refactor-asset-path-verification) as a template

hypothesis: The 5th-tier migration was per-skill (not bulk). propose-boundary was probably migrated in engineering-skills first; the host fork needs a one-line catchup.
summary: Cross-direction sync finding: engineering-skills propose-boundary/scripts/propose.py uses the centralized _common/skill_use.py log_event helper, but host project pnci-pricing's version still has the older local _log_skill_use function. This means at least one host hasn't yet completed the skill-use 5th-tier migration. Either (a) host pnci-pricing should update propose-boundary's script to use _common/skill_use.py, or (b) engineering-skills should retain compatibility for hosts still on the pre-centralization helper. Captured here for visibility; the actual sync may be a one-line edit in the host's script.
title: Host propose-boundary script still has local skill-use logger (pre-_common migration)

hypothesis: An atlas authored once saves the manual Explore-agent passes that real-project observational synthesis tends to require. Provides L3 input surface that /propose-boundary lacks.
summary: Produces a one-page project atlas: one line per top-level subsystem with shape, dependents, dependencies, co-edit neighbors, importance-map tier. Sibling to /map-subsystem at one abstraction higher (L3 instead of L2). Output feeds /propose-boundary (with --scope=project, if added) and /propose-architecture (when that lands). Possible overlap with /propose-folder-reorganization — needs scoping pass first to clarify whether to extend that skill or build separately. Natural output home: a .claude/docs/atlas.md surface authored once + refreshed periodically.
title: /map-project skill — project-level atlas (L3 abstraction)

hypothesis: Without an authored constraints surface, any architecture-level proposal skill will hallucinate vendor-coupling, hot-path assertions, or team-ownership facts. With the surface, a small skill can produce highly contextual recommendations. Pilot: declare one entry, then validate downstream skill output reflects it.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on constraint-aware boundary proposal
summary: Authored surface declaring architectural constraints the code alone can't reveal: (1) tight-integration zones (vendor-coupled code that shouldn't be abstracted — the file's value is co-location of vendor quirks); (2) hot paths (where network hops between modules are unacceptable); (3) failure domains (independent-failure modules, circuit-breakable); (4) team ownership (multi-team adopters). Possibly extends importance-map.md (ADR 0016) as new locator kinds, or a sibling constraints-map.md. Prerequisite for /propose-architecture — completion-trained models will fabricate these signals if not given them.
title: constraints-declaration-surface — authored inputs for constraint-aware architecture

hypothesis: The most valuable architecture insights come from the disagreement between lenses, not from either alone. A skill that surfaces disagreement is much higher-leverage than either lens alone.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on constraint-aware boundary proposal
summary: Higher-abstraction sibling to /propose-boundary. Consumes project atlas (from /map-project) + constraints-declaration-surface, produces three-bucket output: (1) structural-clean seams to act on; (2) structural seams to leave coupled with constraint rationale (vendor-coupling, hot-path proximity, failure-domain co-location); (3) deployment-seam candidates (microservice / library / separate-repo) with constraint evidence (distinct scaling profile, independent failure domain, stable narrow contract, team alignment). Headline value: surfacing DISAGREEMENT between structural and constraint lenses (e.g. 'structural says split, constraint says encapsulate'). Output framed as evidence for a System-tier deliberation chain, not a verdict.
title: /propose-architecture skill — constraint-aware optimal-shape proposal

hypothesis: Multi-team adopters will hit Conway's-Law boundary questions immediately on adoption. An /propose-architecture run with a team-ownership map should produce visibly different recommendations than the same run without one.
origin: host-project conversation 2026-05-14 on team-organization in boundary design
summary: Explicit orthogonal-concern intake for team-ownership boundaries. Conway's Law: organizations design systems mirroring their communication structures. When multiple teams own slices of a codebase, optimal boundaries follow team lines to minimize coordination tax — sometimes overriding structural cleanliness. Inverse case (two teams stepping on one file) is a coordination-tax signal that argues for splitting even when the structural seam is messier. Critical for multi-team adopters; degenerate for single-team projects. Likely shape: a field within constraints-declaration-surface (kind=team-ownership locator + team name), not a separate file.
title: Conway's Law overlay — team-ownership boundaries as architecture force

summary: The ecosystem grew from a Django host: many lint rules, scripts, and skill calibrations carry Django/Python assumptions, so generalizing beyond Django currently falls to whoever ports it (per the existing porting contract in .claude/skills/_common/portability-roadmap.md). Ship a maintained suite of non-Django default lint rules plus skill calibrations per language — TypeScript, Rust, Go, … — each refined by dogfooding real open-source projects in that language, so the pack becomes adoptable out of the box without per-importer porting work. Explicitly backlog, not scheduled — captured as a direction, not a committed plan.
title: Non-Django default lint/skill suites per language, refined via OSS dogfooding

hypothesis: Plan/spec/SKILL.md artifacts are DAGs flattened into numbered lists; the list hides the dependency structure (permitting silent inconsistency) and the parallelism (hiding the critical path). Declaring each stage's inputs and outputs as an explicit graph yields both consistency-checking and critical-path scheduling from one representation. Open question: authoring cost, and whether the graph is hand-authored or inferred from existing stage headings.
summary: Plan, spec, and SKILL.md artifacts are dependency graphs flattened into numbered lists. The list format hides which steps actually depend on which — permitting silent inconsistency (a step consuming an input nothing upstream produced) and hiding what is parallelizable versus on the critical path. Proposal: each stage declares its inputs and outputs so the artifact carries an explicit stage-IO graph. One representation pays twice — it can be mechanically checked (the IO graph must close) and scheduled (critical path = longest dependency chain; everything off it parallelizes). Surfaced by dogfooding this ecosystem's own process: the WS1-WS4 plan run this session presented four workstreams as sequential 1-2-3-4 when WS1/WS2/WS4 were nearly independent, and stated a guessed disposition for specs.py as fact because the prose had no slot to mark that it depended on an upstream scout verdict (which later contradicted it). plan-phased-refactor-skill is the narrow instance — a phase-graph for one boundary refactor; this is the general principle under it. Feeds the instruction-artifact coherence detector: the IO-closure check is only possible once the graph is declared.
title: Dependency-explicit plan and skill artifacts — declare the stage-IO graph, not a numbered list

hypothesis: A SKILL.md / plan / spec is an executable spec written in English with no compiler or test suite to punish internal contradiction. Its coherence is checkable structurally — frontmatter vs body, stage-IO graph closure, reference resolution — with no semantic NLP. Open question: what fraction of real incoherence is structurally detectable versus needs human judgment.
summary: All nine architectural smells in the catalog target host code; none targets the ecosystem's own instruction artifacts — SKILL.md, plans, specs, ADR bodies. Yet those are executable specs written in English, with no compiler or test suite to punish internal contradiction, so they drift freely. Evidence this is a real defect class: this session's framework:django mislabels on map-subsystem and find-omnibus were exactly 'frontmatter claims X, body claims not-X' — find-omnibus's own Scope section states it does not touch Django — and nothing in the catalog would catch it (find-rule-surface-drift checks the doc table against the filesystem, find-comment-drift checks comments against code; neither checks a skill artifact against itself). Proposal: a SUSPECT detector — candidate smell 10 — checking instruction artifacts for structural coherence: frontmatter agrees with body, every stage consumes only inputs produced upstream (the stage-IO graph closes), every referenced skill/file/path resolves, claims stated as fact versus assumption are distinguished. Deliberately structural, not semantic — no NLP, no 'understand causal flow'; give prose a type-checker, not a brain. decisions.py audit/link-check — a working consistency checker for ADRs, wired into CI this session — is the proven prototype to generalize. Instruction-artifact analog of system-coherence-drift-detector (which does the same at the code level). Depends on dependency-explicit-artifacts for the stage-IO-closure check.
title: Instruction-artifact coherence detector (smell 10) — a SUSPECT pass for the ecosystem's own SKILL.md / plan / spec prose

hypothesis: Code is reconciled, not derived: the docs-to-code transform is a relation, so the graph can propagate dirtiness deterministically but cannot regenerate content. Open question — what fraction of reconciliation is safely automatable as detect-and-propose versus needs gated human acceptance.
summary: Model the project as a typed DAG so a change reveals everything it affects, including docs. Three node tiers: source (ADRs, rules, style guides, hand-written subsystem docs — authored, never regenerated); derived docs (indexes, catalogs, dashboards — pure functions of their inputs, regenerate freely, the dashboard.md regen already works this way); reconciled (code, and SKILL.md prose). Authority is one-way (docs win as intent) but generation is not — code cannot be re-rendered from docs because the docs-to-code transform is a relation not a function, and code accumulates underdetermined decisions docs never captured. The graph therefore propagates typed dirtiness, not content: changing a style guide marks dependents style-dirty but requirements-clean, scoping and cost-routing each reconciliation. Reconciliation is build-system-style invalidate-then-rebuild where rebuild is LLM-or-human judgment, not a deterministic compile. Code-to-docs is covered by decision-extraction/case-law as a promotion — lifting an implicit decision to an explicit source node, React's lift-state-up move — which keeps the graph acyclic. Passive v0 is near-term and cheap: extract edges that already exist (Python imports for code-to-code; ADR applies_to for rule-to-file, which decisions.py link-check already parses and validates) into one queryable place, mark dirty, show blast radius. The active reconciliation engine is the genuine future undertaking and is model-dependent. Feasible now only because LLM labor removes the human doc-rot failure that always killed doc-driven systems; but automatic must mean detect-and-propose, never auto-apply, since auto-applying many LLM rewrites unsupervised rebuilds the vibe-coded disaster at machine speed. Generalizes dependency-explicit-artifacts from within-artifact stage-IO to across-artifact doc-to-code dependencies.
title: Docs-to-code dependency graph — typed DAG with one-way authority and dirtiness propagation

hypothesis: The comprehension tax is dominated by cacheable components (repo-shape and file-digest), so caching the MAP artifact recovers most of it with no context-rot cost; batching only helps the fix stage, only behind characterization tests, and only within a model-dependent budget calibrated by differential testing against the separated baseline.
summary: A planner that compiles an optimal execution plan for a set of skill invocations, attacking the comprehension tax — the repeated cost of re-establishing repo and file understanding once per skill per file, which was the real time sink in this ecosystem's multi-week build. Decompose the tax into four parts: repo-shape and file-digest are cacheable (the MAP-tier artifact is the natural cache); cross-finding synthesis is currently performed by no skill (the orchestrator does it by hand); fix-context blast-radius is irreducible. Lever priority: first cache shared comprehension (MAP as a required input, not an optional doc), then parallelize detection into clean windows, and only last batch fixes — the smallest and riskiest win. Detection and fixing have opposite batching profiles: detection is independent and should be parallelized (clean context per scout, which is anti-context-rot), fixing is interacting and must share one context but only behind characterization tests, within a context-rot budget that behaves like a scheduler issue width. Tests are externalized comprehension — they let the model forget, which is what makes a fix batch fit in a window. Run regimes differ: iterative (pre-commit or PR, diff-scoped — the SUSPECT tier is not yet diff-scoped, a real gap), major (full-system analysis, MAP tier), and merge (an iterative run plus cross-branch artifact-staleness detection). The separated dev bundle is both the compiler source and the test oracle: differential-test the batched distribution bundle against it the way -O2 output is tested against -O0; the distribution bundle is compiled for a target model, since safe batch width is model-dependent and must be calibrated, not guessed. The planner also absorbs cross-finding synthesis post-run. Endorsed in conversation as a good idea.
title: Skill-execution planner — a scheduler over the skill graph that reduces the comprehension tax

hypothesis: Comprehension-tax component one — per-skill repo-shape re-derivation — dominates total run cost; an enriched ledger carrying cost fields can confirm or refute this, turning a current guess into a measurement.
summary: Today reports/_meta/effectiveness.jsonl records per-run counts only (findings_total and buckets). Enrich the schema to retain per-finding traces — code excerpt, detector output, scout rationale, and the verified label including hard negatives — plus cost fields (tokens, wall-clock, context size at decision points). One small change to an artifact that already exists, with three payoffs: it makes the comprehension tax measurable instead of anecdotal; it supplies the calibration data the skill-execution-planner needs to fit safe per-model batch budgets; and it becomes a synthetic-data corpus of verified architectural-judgment traces with hard negatives — the rare and valuable kind of training data, unlike generated code which is worthless because the internet is already saturated with it. Concrete evidence the value is currently discarded: the find-omnibus scan scan-20260516-020044 produced four training-grade hard negatives (the facets_not_domains bucket — product_topology.py and three detector files, each with a facet-vs-domain rationale explaining why it looks like an omnibus but is not), and the ledger kept only the bucket count, not the rationale. This is the smallest and most concrete of the three linked intakes and the right near-term first step.
title: Verified-judgment-trace ledger — enrich effectiveness.jsonl from a per-run tally to a per-finding corpus

hypothesis: A lightweight complexity-hotspot scan gives reviewers and refactor planners a cheap first-pass lead list without turning heuristic findings into automatic optimization work.
summary: Adds a read-only SUSPECT skill for algorithmic, ORM, and structural complexity leads. It scans Python code for nested loops, membership scans, sort-in-loop patterns, QuerySet or manager calls inside loops, and high-branch functions, then writes standard report artifacts. The useful lesson from dogfooding was that performance scanners need conservative receiver heuristics and measurement-first recommendations so they generate leads rather than confident rewrites.
title: Find complexity hotspots skill

summary: Built from a host-project request inspired by Kappaemme-git/codex-complexity-optimizer, but adapted to this ecosystem as a read-only find-* skill with frontmatter, PNCI/general reading notes, fixtures, smoke coverage, report output, and catalog/kernel registration. Dogfood on site-intelligence paths caught and fixed noisy dict.get and QuerySet-iteration false positives, added max-findings validation, and kept the final recommendation language measurement-first.
Adopted into engineering-skills-2 by adding .claude/skills/find-complexity-hotspots plus skill-catalog and quality-kernel references; validation passed with smoke, ruff, and skill_meta lint.

hypothesis: Context-composition and side-effect/blast-radius analysis are two query directions over one typed, weighted, two-speed project knowledge graph; building that graph as an always-derived first-class substrate lets the quality skills become queries instead of scanners, and lets an agent classify task triviality (= bounded blast radius) instead of defensively over-engineering.
summary: Captures where the code-quality skill ecosystem should converge: an always-current, easy-to-parse, typed-and-weighted project knowledge graph as the shared substrate. Core thesis from a design conversation. (1) The two long-standing branches are the same datastore viewed from two directions: branch 1 (reduce the exploration needed to be sure of context) is a backward-plus-neighborhood walk from a task seed; branch 2 (be sure of the magnitude of a change side-effects) is a forward walk from the same seed. One graph, two traversals. (2) Triviality classification falls out for free: trivial means bounded blast radius, so an agent cannot safely call a task trivial without branch 2 — the over-engineering failure mode (the Claude-vs-Codex meme) is the rational behavior of an agent that cannot see the boundary of its own certainty. (3) Graph design: nodes are symbols, files, models, routes, tasks, contracts, domain terms, ADRs, tests, known-issues; edges are typed and layered by automatability — static edges (calls, imports, refs) are auto-derived and genuinely always-current; dynamic/registry edges (Celery dispatch-by-name, URL conf, signals, template-context) are dynamic in general but enumerable per project and declared; semantic/contract edges (must-stay-format-equivalent, serialized-into-export) and state edges (a computation change retroactively reinterprets persisted rows, the hardest class, almost nothing catches it) must be declared and accreted on surprise. (4) The honest tool output is the boundary between what the graph is sure of and what it is not, not a false-precise list of exact side-effects — and that boundary is what removes the incentive to over-engineer. (5) Two-speed freshness: always-up-to-date is honest only for the auto layer; declared layers carry per-edge provenance, confidence, and staleness markers, because a confident-looking graph that is actually guessing is worse than no graph. (6) Edges are weighted as well as typed — risk-weighting is what turns a 40-hit dump into one ranked answer, the way a senior engineer checks the 2 dangerous edges and ignores 38. (7) The reframe for the skill ecosystem: skills stop being scanners that re-derive structure and emit stale reports, and become queries and interpreters over the graph — MAP is a rendered view, SUSPECT is a graph predicate, EXPLAIN renders subgraph-plus-semantics, REFACTOR is a graph diff, GUARD is a graph invariant. Five verbs, one substrate. (8) Anti-rot discipline: derive what you can so it cannot drift from code; co-locate the declared edges next to the code they describe (a contract annotation by the function) rather than centralizing them into a new rot magnet. (9) Easy-to-parse is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a boring universal queryable format makes the graph infrastructure (PR review becomes a before/after graph diff, onboarding and the subsystem atlas become renders, health metrics become queries); a bespoke store makes it a silo. (10) Migration trigger from the current markdown-shard era (ADRs, precedents.yml, known-issues.md, find-* reports, CONTEXT.md, importance-map.md — the correct early prototype): migrate to a real store when agents start failing to join across the shards, i.e. when manual cross-referencing cost exceeds the cost of paying for the store once. Closely related to docs-to-code-dependency-graph (the docs-to-code slice of the same graph, with dirtiness propagation) and skill-execution-planner (the graph is the comprehension-tax cache that planner needs).
title: Code knowledge graph as the convergence substrate for the quality skills

hypothesis: Making the target architecture an explicit, drift-checkable artifact lets the existing incremental tiers be aimed: re-architecting becomes accumulable rather than one high-risk transform, and behavior-preserving refactors stop polishing a system inside an expired frame.
summary: The ecosystem has durable artifacts for point decisions (ADRs), for features (specs), and for CURRENT state (map-subsystem, the map-project atlas, importance-map) — but nothing holds DESIRED whole-system state. The target architecture lives only in a human head, which is why behavior-preserving refactors can only rearrange furniture inside the founding frame and can never aim at a better one (the conversation phrase: software does not rot, it outlives its founding frame). Proposal: a standing, durable target-architecture artifact (Shape B) — a sibling to the current-state atlas — plus a drift metric defined as diff(current atlas, Shape B), computable as a query once the knowledge-graph index exists. Effect: re-architecting stops being a single high-risk transform and becomes a direction that many safe small moves (the refactor tier, the System-tier chain, /decide) accumulate toward, each scored by whether it reduces drift. Distinct from propose-architecture-skill, which generates a one-shot proposal — this idea PERSISTS the chosen target and measures distance to it continuously, and propose-architecture output is the natural seed for authoring the artifact. Distinct from system-coherence-drift-detector, which measures intrinsic coherence rather than distance from a declared target. Distinct from map-project, which captures current state only. Scoped but parked: worth exploring, no build slot yet; the index keystone (code-knowledge-graph-substrate) should land first.
title: Target-architecture artifact — persist desired Shape B plus a drift metric the incremental tiers aim at

summary: Sequencing note from a design conversation (host project pnci-pricing). Of the convergence ideas, the derived knowledge-graph index is the keystone and should be built first, deliberately conservatively: keep the markdown/JSONL/YAML shards (ADRs, precedents.yml, known-issues, find-* reports, CONTEXT.md, importance-map, the idea ledger) as the git-diffable human-readable source of truth, and add the index only as a disposable derived cache rebuilt from those shards. SQLite with recursive CTEs is almost certainly enough for the dependency-graph traversals — a bespoke graph DB is not warranted yet and would trade away the shard-level diffability that is the ecosystem ethos. Keystone argument: churn detection, per-idea coverage audits, and target-architecture drift measurement each otherwise re-derive the same cross-shard joins by hand on every run, so one index pays for itself across all three. New framing the conversation added: even with flat files retained, specialized query and update tooling over them is itself the deliverable — the mental transform of a shard into a usable frame is a comprehension tax, and that tax is a direct cause of AI-agent failure, disproportionately so in high-velocity vibe coding where no human rechecks the details, so the index is a correctness and safety surface, not merely a speed optimization. Broader intent: candidate to productize for people doing too much vibe coding; the index is the load-bearing piece of any such product and will need real optimization work. Addendum — the authority-gradient framing. docs-to-code is the ideal case not because traversal is one-way (side-effect analysis always needs both directions plus sibling expansion) but because every edge carries a designated authority side: the doc declares intent, the code conforms. That single property buys monotone one-way dirtiness propagation, near-statically-declared edges, and — the crux — findings that are actionable rather than merely alarming. An edge with an authority label yields an answer (code B violated contract C); an edge without one yields only a question (A and B diverged — which is wrong?). The dangerous edges in the general code graph (format-equivalent peer writers, ordering assumptions) are dangerous precisely because they are directionless: no designated authority. Key reframe: the messy code graph is not a different graph from docs-to-code — it is the same graph before its implicit peer-couplings have been promoted to authored contracts. Contract extraction (what the refactor skills already do) is exactly the operation that converts one undirected high-risk edge into two clean docs-to-code edges, by introducing an authority node both sides derive from. So docs-to-code-dependency-graph is not a sibling idea but a BAND of this substrate — the subset of edges that already have a clean authority gradient; the substrate is the whole graph including the not-yet-authoritative edges. This yields a concrete architectural health metric instead of a vibe: the fraction of risky coupling that has a designated authority. A codebase where every dangerous edge is authority-labelled has cheap freshness and answerable side-effects; one full of directionless peer edges makes every change a guess (the over-engineering failure mode, structurally). The graph measures that fraction; the maintenance loop's job is to raise it — push high-risk coupling from the undirected end toward the directed-authoritative end. Implication for reconciling the two ledger entries: treat docs-to-code-dependency-graph as the directed-authoritative band of code-knowledge-graph-substrate, not a separate artifact.
